reason: The cited evidence does not directly support the key premises. E3 shows that aging AlCoCrFeNi at 500–600°C forms grain-boundary precipitates, not just ordered clusters, and E1/E2/E4 are about different alloy systems or mechanisms and do not address local ordering in AlCoCrFeNi. The hypothesis misrepresents or overlooks the precipitate formation documented in E3.
premises: AlCoCrFeNi can be retained as a fully disordered single-phase solid solution
Aging at 500–600°C induces local chemical ordering at grain boundaries without forming intermetallic precipitates
These ordered clusters reduce plastic accommodation and promote brittle intergranular fracture
The embrittlement mechanism is distinct from conventional precipitation-driven embrittlement
